clue.text: Conflict among comedians?

parts.note: read literally, a fight between funny people, since wits are clever jokers; really an exchange of clever retorts

explanation.definitionFit: A contest of clever repartee is a fight fought with jokes and quick minds, which is what comedians trade.

clue.text: Relief for the visually handicap, ped

definitions.text: Relief for the visually handicap, ped

parts.words: Relief for the visually handicap, ped
parts.note: relief here is raised lettering, as in a relief carving, read by touch rather than help or comfort

explanation.definitionFit: The tactile writing system of raised dots lets blind people read with their fingertips, a script in relief.

clue.text: Tailless monkey, rodents or birds

indicators.note: without its tail, so the final letter of the monkey's name is dropped

parts.note: the titi is a small South American monkey
mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A list of small animals: a monkey missing its tail, some rodents, or birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small songbirds such as blue tits and great tits are collectively known by this old plural.

clue.text: Rather slow when dealing with notes

definitions.text: Rather slow when dealing with notes

parts.words: Rather slow when dealing with notes
parts.note: a musical tempo marking: somewhat slow, used when playing written music

explanation.definitionFit: The Italian tempo direction means fairly slow, a little quicker than largo, an instruction found in scores.

clue.text: Award so revolutionary a vehicle

indicators.note: turning round, so the little word so is written back to front

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A prize goes to a radical new kind of motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette given to film-makers is universally known by this nickname.

clue.text: Wesley sent in perhaps because ofthe rain

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged some other way, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: Wes is the usual short form of the name Wesley
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Wesley was sent indoors, maybe because it was raining.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten Wesley to its pet form WES, add SENT, and rearrange the seven letters at the signal 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain leaves everything damp, so the rain is equated with the state of being soaked.

clue.text: Call it oriental wood destroyer

parts.note: to call something is to term it, to give it a name
taken as written
E for eastern, which is what oriental means

explanation.surface: Someone names an exotic eastern insect that ruins timber.
explanation.definitionFit: These pale social insects eat timber and can bring down houses by hollowing beams.

clue.text: Angry part of a representative sample

parts.note: cross means angry or annoyed
a section is a part of something

explanation.surface: An irate portion of a typical selection of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice through a population that reflects all its groups is a typical, balanced sampling.

clue.text: One who responds to a nuclear device

definitions.meaning: a person who reacts to something
the vessel in a power station where atomic fission is controlled

explanation.definitionFit: Someone reacting is literally a reactor; separately, an atomic pile in a power station bears the same name.

clue.text: He provides food on the rickety terrace

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man serves meals out on a wobbly patio.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who supplies meals for events and functions is a professional food supplier.

clue.text: On all sides but not at the front or back?

definitions.text: On all sides but not at the front or back?

parts.words: On all sides but not at the front or back?
parts.note: a playful description: everywhere, yet only on the two flanks, port and starboard rather than fore and aft

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means everywhere, in all directions, yet literally names only the two flanks of something.

clue.text: Sprite initially is mischievous and egotistical

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word Sprite

parts.note: elfish means impish and mischievous, like an elf

explanation.surface: A fairy-like sprite is naughty and thinks only of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being self-centred means putting your own interests first, which is the meaning here.

clue.text: Dancing when drunk?

definitions.meaning: performing a reel, the lively Scottish dance
staggering about as one does when intoxicated

explanation.definitionFit: Doing a Scottish reel is one sense; lurching and staggering from too much drink is the other.

clue.text: A Scandinavian to feed the cattle?

definitions.meaning: a root vegetable grown as fodder for livestock

explanation.definitionFit: A person from Sweden shares the name with the yellow turnip often grown as cattle fodder.

clue.text: New trains, about ten, staying only for a short time

definitions.text: staying only for a short time

indicators.note: new indicates the letters take a fresh form, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some new trains, around ten of them, are only in service briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of TRAINS and TEN together; 'about' merely joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passing or temporary stays briefly before moving on, the sense of a short visit.

clue.text: Abolition meant somehow to in elude Sally on the way up

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece goes within the other
somehow says the letters are rearranged in some fashion
in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a Sally Lunn is a sweet teacake from Bath, so the name gives its partner Lunn

explanation.surface: A cancellation was somehow planned to involve someone called Sally as she climbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns MEANT into AMENT; 'on the way up' reverses LUNN to NNUL, which goes in after the A. A Sally Lunn is a large British teacake.
explanation.definitionFit: Annulment is the cancelling or abolishing of something, such as a law or a marriage.

clue.text: Tropic island produce

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is farm produce, grain

explanation.surface: A tropical island and the crops it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern line of latitude is the Tropic of Capricorn, so the word alone names that tropic.

clue.text: High rise flat

parts.note: not an apartment in a tower block but an elevated stretch of level land

explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is a raised expanse of level ground, so it is both elevated and level.

clue.text: I translate bear in Spanish and Portuguese

indicators.note: to translate is to turn into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone renders the word for bear into the languages of Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holding Spain and Portugal is Iberia, so things from both countries share this adjective.

clue.text: Nothing right during the short day for a stupid person

indicators.note: during means within a period, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday
O is a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing went right on Monday, thanks to a foolish colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit or fool is someone of low intelligence; the word is an insult for a slow-witted person.

clue.text: Ram tusk of another animal

indicators.note: another form of the words, so their letters are rearranged into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A ram's horn-like tusk belongs to some other creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A large North American water rodent with a musky smell is an animal of riverbanks.

clue.text: Whale or sea-monster, say, in choppy Ural

indicators.note: in places the middle letters inside the shuffled river name
choppy water is rough and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
say signals that the monster's name is used for its sound, spelt differently

parts.note: an orc is a mythical sea monster

explanation.surface: A whale, or some sea monster, appears in the rough waters of the Ural river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choppy' turns URAL into RUAL; ORC, said aloud, is written ORQ and goes in after the R. 'or' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of baleen whales with throat grooves, including the blue and fin whales.

clue.text: I am taking a very long time with lines on figurative illustrations

parts.note: contracted to I'm
an age is a very long time
RY, short for railway, is a crossword staple for lines

explanation.surface: Someone takes ages over lines of poetry full of picturesque description.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language that paints pictures in the reader's mind, such as metaphor and simile.

clue.text: Ascetic bear appears before mid-morning

parts.note: Yogi Bear is the cartoon bear
the middle letter of the word morning is N

explanation.surface: A holy man in self-denial sees a bear show up before mid-morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu practitioner of yoga who lives austerely is a self-denying holy man.

clue.text: Quinquennial of the ceremony of purification

definitions.meaning: every five years, from the Roman lustrum, a five-year period
relating to a cleansing rite, the Roman lustration

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman lustrum was both a five-year census period and a purification sacrifice, so the adjective covers both.

clue.text: Requiring new engine round about fifth Tuesday

indicators.note: going round about something puts it inside, so one piece wraps the other
new means a fresh form, so the letters are rearranged
the fifth letter of the word Tuesday is taken

explanation.surface: A new engine is needed by roughly the fifth Tuesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanting or lacking something essential is the same as having a requirement for it.

clue.text: Spike's handy cover prevents sound penetrating

parts.note: a spike of grain such as wheat is an ear
a muff is a fur tube covering the hands

explanation.surface: A dog called Spike has a cover over its paw to keep out noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike is a grain head (an EAR of corn), not a name; the definition describes what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Padded coverings worn over the ears block out cold and noise.

clue.text: Cumulative number of athletes in the race?

definitions.text: Cumulative number of athletes in the race?

parts.words: Cumulative number of athletes in the race?
parts.note: read literally, a head-count of runners competing; really a sum continually updated

explanation.definitionFit: A tally kept up to date as each new figure is added is a cumulative sum.
